properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live TLS protocol config, changeable here: these scripts tee-write nginx vhost/stream configs (bonus.btcpaysetdomain.sh: `| sudo tee /etc/nginx/sites-available/btcpayserver`) that pin deprecated TLSv1/TLSv1.1 alongside TLSv1.2 — and BTCPayServer/electrs variants omit TLSv1.3 entirely. TLS 1.0/1.1 admit non-forward-secret suites and downgrade attacks; also blocks any move to hybrid PQ key exchange which requires TLS 1.3.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TLS 1.1 (deprecated by RFC 8996) and TLS 1.2 both admit classical-KEX sessions; hybrid PQ groups require TLS 1.3. The D rating comes from the TLSv1.1 floor in the BTCPayServer guides/scripts. Changeable here — one directive per config block.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live TLS cipher-suite policy, changeable here: the Mozilla 'intermediate' list applied to every nginx vhost these scripts write (BTCPayServer, subdomain forwarders, nostr relay, mempool). PQ-relevant core: all key exchanges it permits are ECDHE-RSA/ECDSA or DHE-RSA/DSS — Shor-vulnerable, harvest-now-decrypt-later on passively captured traffic; TLS 1.3-only + hybrid X25519MLKEM768 groups is the migration. The !aNULL:!eNULL:!EXPORT:!DES:!RC4:!3DES:!MD5:!PSK tail correctly excludes weak ciphers (wh

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: One cipher policy shared by every BTCPay vhost; the ECDSA (ALG-710f61f0) and ECDH (ALG-c9ffc8a8) objects carry the per-algorithm readings of the same string. Note ssl_ciphers constrains only TLS<=1.2. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live PKI asset, changeable here: each script generates a throwaway self-signed RSA-2048 certificate (unencrypted key, -nodes, localhost.key/localhost.crt) for the electrs Electrum-RPC TLS endpoint. Self-signed = no chain of trust (clients must be forced to pin/trust it manually); the 1825-day variant on line 156 leaves a 5-year RSA-2048 cert in place — RSA key/cert is Shor-vulnerable and the TLS handshake it serves is harvest-now-decrypt-later.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency asset, changeable here: the Electrum wallet helper installs libsecp256k1-0, the Bitcoin signature curve library. Electrum/Bitcoin keys and addresses are secp256k1 ECDSA — Shor-vulnerable; all funds controlled by this node's wallets become forgeable/spendable by a quantum attacker. The curve is fixed by the Bitcoin protocol (not changeable here without a chain-level soft fork), so this asset is 'observable here, replaceable only by the network'.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RaspiBlitz deployment repo: these scripts generate every nginx vhost on the node (BTCPay, electrum, RTL, mempool, nostr, custom sites) and two curl client floors. Changeable here. Weakest floors: electrs modules and nginx/bonus.SSL_for_RTL.sh pin TLSv1 TLSv1.1 TLSv1.2 (TLS 1.0/1.1 deprecated by RFC 8996); nginx subdomain scripts pin the modern TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3 floor. No ssl_ecdh_curves/ssl_groups directive anywhere configures PQ key-exchange groups.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TLS 1.3 is the only protocol where hybrid PQ key-exchange groups (X25519MLKEM768) can negotiate in nginx; enabling it is prerequisite, not sufficient — no group/curves directive in this repo configures PQ groups, so sessions remain classical-KEX. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: These lists are the Mozilla 'intermediate' list applied to every vhost; the ECDSA suites share the same ssl_ciphers string as the ECDHE object (one cipher policy, two algorithm aspects: auth + kex). Migration needs PQ cert signing at the CA (ML-DSA/SLH-DSA) plus ML-DSA server certs. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDHE is the harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure for all traffic through these vhosts (BTCPay payments, electrum wallets, RTL, mempool). Migration: TLS 1.3 + hybrid X25519MLKEM768 groups (nginx with OpenSSL 3.5+). Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live cipher policy component, changeable here: the nginx ssl_ciphers list enables ECDHE/DHE-AES128-GCM and AES128-SHA/SHA256 suites for BTCPayServer and the subdomain forwarders. Grover halves this to a 64-bit margin — below the AES-256 floor CNSA 2.0 sets for post-quantum. Not urgent on its own; captured sessions remain safe symmetrically, but the key exchange protecting them is not.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live cipher policy component, changeable here: authenticated-encryption GCM suites are the preferred bulk ciphers of every nginx vhost these scripts write. Sound mode choice; graded at the AES-128 floor because both 128- and 256-bit GCM suites are enabled (AES-256-GCM-SHA384 variants are the CNSA 2.0 target).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live cipher policy component, changeable here: AES256-GCM-SHA384 / AES256-SHA256/SHA suites enabled in the same nginx ssl_ciphers lists — the strongest symmetric posture in the repo (128-bit quantum margin under Grover), matching the CNSA 2.0 target; the surrounding ECDHE/DHE key exchange remains the quantum weakness.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Chain material of the same certificate; nginx consumes it separately for stapling verification. CA chain algorithm is Let's Encrypt-controlled (RSA-2048 ISRG intermediates); the reference itself is changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shor recovers this key from the public certificate; rotation is a cheap certbot reissue. Same reference written by bonus.btcpaysetdomain.sh:152 and btcpay_to_blitz.sh:307 ($YOUR_DOMAIN). Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Quantum-unsafe either way (RSA or ECDSA under Shor). The same deployment is written live by BTCPayServer/bonus.btcpaysetdomain.sh:151 and btcpay_to_blitz.sh:306 ($YOUR_DOMAIN), and every nginx/ subdomain script references the same certbot material per-service ($SUBDOMAIN/$DOMAIN_NAME). Changeable here: certbot --key-type at reissue; PQ issuance is gated on Let's Encrypt (vendor).
